route.name: Tripoli-Homs Railway
route.notes: The 'missed connection': the Lebanese and Syrian networks never fully integrated here, partly because of the gauge differences around Tripoli/Homs.  [gauge_mm] GAUGE IS A TWO-ERA PUZZLE, not a simple error — sources conflict, so verify: (a) the ORIGINAL 1911 DHP Homs–Tripoli branch appears to have been 1,050 mm NARROW gauge (Wikipedia), which would have meant yet another gauge break at Homs against the standard-gauge Aleppo line; (b) a STANDARD-gauge (1,435 mm) connection to Tripoli came later — the WWII HBT coastal line reached Tripoli on 18 Dec 1942, and the post-war Syrian (CFS) standard-gauge network served Homs. The project’s 1,435 mm is defensible for the LATER standard-gauge era but likely NOT for the original 1911 branch.  [route] Runs inland from Tripoli (El Mina) through the HOMS GAP / Akkar plain to Homs, where it joined the Syrian network (Damascus–Homs–Hama–Aleppo). Intermediate stations are NOT documented in the consulted sources (a research gap); likely candidates on the corridor include Abou Halqa, the Akkar plain, and Tell Kalakh (Syria) — unverified.
route.history: A DHP branch linking the Mediterranean port of Tripoli inland to Homs (on the Syrian standard-gauge network toward Hama and Aleppo), through the Homs Gap — the natural lowland pass between the Lebanon and coastal mountain ranges.
